items.title:
Lithium Iron Phosphate
Energy Storage Safety
items.desc: As China advances its carbon-peaking and carbon-neutrality goals, rapid photovoltaic deployment creates new challenges for grid stability because solar output fluctuates. Lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries are widely used to support renewable energy, but safe operation depends on the entire storage system—not just the cells. This project draws on the national standard GB 51048-2025 to examine safety hazards across seven core modules and corresponding standardized prevention measures. It considers how failures in cells, battery packs, control systems, thermal management, fire protection, and site infrastructure can trigger cascading thermal runaway, providing a theoretical reference for engineering design and routine operation and maintenance.
